subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers fail closed on all persisted ownerless session rows across create, patch, reset, and delete, or must an explicit migration or narrower compatibility policy precede enforcement?
rationale: The branch changes access to persisted session state at a plugin isolation boundary, and source inspection cannot determine whether legacy ownerless rows are intentionally accessible or require an upgrade path.

options.title: Approve consistent fail-closed enforcement
options.body: Treat ownerless rows as having no plugin authority, use one canonical guard across every mutation and parent-use path, and document the upgrade behavior.

options.title: Require an ownership migration
options.body: Define a safe doctor or operator-driven migration for affected rows before runtime enforcement, without adding a steady-state fallback reader.

options.title: Narrow the initial enforcement
options.body: Land only behavior with an unambiguous existing ownership contract and defer ownerless-row handling to a coordinated follow-up.

recommendation.title: Approve consistent fail-closed enforcement
recommendation.body: Treat ownerless rows as having no plugin authority, use one canonical guard across every mutation and parent-use path, and document the upgrade behavior.
